## ✨ Added

- Zero-knowledge (end-to-end) encryption: your browser encrypts every file with `XChaCha20-Poly1305` (libsodium `crypto_secretstream`, 64 KiB chunks) before the upload starts. The content key never reaches the server. In link mode it lives only in the URL `#fragment`, which never appears in a request line. In password mode it is wrapped with an Argon2id-derived key and only the wrapped blob is stored. The filename and content type are encrypted inside the blob too, so the server sees nothing but ciphertext and its length.
- Any file size: encryption streams through the Origin Private File System (OPFS) and uploads resume with tus, so the size limit is your disk, not your RAM. Downloads decrypt and stream to disk through a service worker. Browsers without OPFS or streaming fall back to encrypting in memory for files up to 500 MB, and larger files get a clear message. That includes any plain-HTTP page, where the browser exposes no `navigator.storage`. For big files, the clipboard and streaming downloads, open featherdrop over HTTPS (see the Reverse Proxy section of the README).
- Inline preview runs entirely in the browser: images and PDFs are decrypted on the download page and rendered from an in-memory `blob:` URL, so the server no longer serves any inline route. Only inert types are shown (raster images and PDF, never SVG or HTML), and the check runs on the decrypted file.

## ⚡ Improved

- featherdrop is zero-knowledge: files are end-to-end encrypted in your browser before they leave it, so the server only ever stores opaque ciphertext. It can't read your files, their names or their types, even if it wanted to. This is a breaking change to the crypto model, and the points below explain what it means for an upgrade.
- The server is a plain ciphertext store: it keeps and serves the opaque blob as it is, enforces the expiry and the download limit, and never does any cryptography. The `GET` download response is raw bytes, so no key or password ever shows up in a request to the server.
- Server master-key mode is gone, because a server that can decrypt with its own key contradicts the zero-knowledge model. New shares use link mode (key in the `#fragment`) or password mode.
- Shares created before 1.6.0 keep working until they expire: featherdrop reads them with the previous scheme. The data model handles both formats and the migration is additive, so you don't need to do anything on upgrade. Ports, the `/data` volume and the configuration stay the same.
- The key is in the link: a zero-knowledge link only decrypts if the whole URL is copied, including the part after `#`. A truncated link can't be recovered, because the server never had the key.
- The privacy copy in the app, the README and the template now makes the zero-knowledge claim and replaces the earlier "encrypted at rest" wording.
- New isolated client modules: `lib/e2e/crypto.ts` (the crypto core), `blob-layout.ts` (the framed blob format), `opfs-scratch.ts`, `stream-download.ts` with `public/sw-download.js`, `pipeline.ts`, and the upload and download flows. Each is unit-tested in Node with libsodium, including a full encrypt, blob, decrypt round trip.
- A new CI end-to-end test starts the built app and drives a real browser through encrypt, upload, share link, decrypt and download on every push. It checks that the output is byte-identical and that the inline preview works.
